(1) the disk is not a rigidly rotating structure but rather a structure that is able to oscillate in response to a perturbation; (2) the disk oscillations are damped, but the damping time is long enough that the disk may oscillate for many vertical crossing periods; and (3) the damping time is sensitive to the disk model and the halo potential.

the Galactic disk is capable of supporting undamped oscillations, and these oscillations may persist for long time periods.
